headline_marked: 8 Bangladeshis among 16 [[migrant workers detained in Indonesia]]
headline: 8 Bangladeshis among 16 migrant workers detained in Indonesia
summary: The workers were intercepted by the Indonesian Navy while attempting to enter the Riau province illegally from Malaysia via speedboat.
details: The Indonesian Navy detained 16 migrant workers on Monday while they were attempting to enter Indonesia's Riau province illegally from Malaysia.
Among those detained are eight Bangladeshi nationals and eight Indonesian citizens.
The group used a twin-engine speedboat to cross the border illegally, reaching the coast of Pantai Purnama in the West Dumai district of Dumai city.

Colonel Agung N. Kusumaji, head of the Dumai Naval Base, stated that the operation was based on intelligence reports received Sunday evening regarding a plan to enter through an illegal jetty at Pantai Mutiara.
Following the intelligence, a joint team was ordered to monitor and intercept the group in the waters and coastal areas of Pantai Purnama.

The operation was led by Captain Wahyu Widhi Bidayat, head of the naval base's intelligence unit, and involved multiple naval units, including the Quick Response Team and the Intelmar maritime intelligence units.
The naval teams departed from the Sungai Dumai Maritime Potential Post to carry out the interception.
caption:
8 Bangladeshis and 8 Indonesians caught attempting to enter Indonesia illegally from Malaysia.

The Indonesian Navy detained 16 migrant workers on Monday while they were attempting to enter Indonesia's Riau province illegally from Malaysia.

Among those detained are eight Bangladeshi nationals and eight Indonesian citizens.

The group used a twin-engine speedboat to cross the border illegally, reaching the coast of Pantai Purnama in the West Dumai district of Dumai city.

Colonel Agung N. Kusumaji, head of the Dumai Naval Base, stated that the operation was based on intelligence reports received Sunday evening regarding a plan to enter through an illegal jetty at Pantai Mutiara.

Following the intelligence, a joint team was ordered to monitor and intercept the group in the waters and coastal areas of Pantai Purnama.

The operation was led by Captain Wahyu Widhi Bidayat, head of the naval base's intelligence unit, and involved multiple naval units, including the Quick Response Team and the Intelmar maritime intelligence units.

The naval teams departed from the Sungai Dumai Maritime Potential Post to carry out the interception.

headline_marked: 7-year-old [[kidnapped in Dhaka's Shewrapara]], CCTV shows woman taking child
headline: 7-year-old kidnapped in Dhaka's Shewrapara, CCTV shows woman taking child
summary: Police have identified a suspect woman in CCTV footage, but the child remains missing after two days. No ransom demands have been made so far.
details: A seven-year-old boy was kidnapped from the Shewrapara area of Kafrul Police Station in Dhaka on Thursday afternoon, September 3.
CCTV footage from the scene shows a woman, aged 20-22, taking the child by the hand from a lane next to the Health Lab Diagnostic Center. The child appeared to be familiar with the woman.
The suspect, wearing a black salwar-kameez, was seen boarding a rickshaw with the boy. Police tracked the rickshaw's movement through multiple cameras up to Agargaon, but lost the trail after that.
Kafrul Police Station OC Saifull Islam stated that raids are being conducted in various locations, including rickshaw garages, to find the vehicle and the child.
Despite two days passing, no ransom demands have been made, leaving the motive for the kidnapping unclear.
According to police headquarters, between January and July, 474 GDs were filed for missing children aged 1-9, with 68 still missing.
For children aged 10-17, 15,243 GDs were filed in the same period, with 1,970 still missing, totaling 2,038 missing children in that age range.
caption:
A 7-year-old boy vanished from Dhaka's Shewrapara. CCTV caught the moment a woman led him away.

A seven-year-old boy was kidnapped from the Shewrapara area of Kafrul Police Station in Dhaka on Thursday afternoon, September 3.

CCTV footage from the scene shows a woman, aged 20-22, taking the child by the hand from a lane next to the Health Lab Diagnostic Center. The child appeared to be familiar with the woman.

The suspect, wearing a black salwar-kameez, was seen boarding a rickshaw with the boy. Police tracked the rickshaw's movement through multiple cameras up to Agargaon, but lost the trail after that.

Kafrul Police Station OC Saifull Islam stated that raids are being conducted in various locations, including rickshaw garages, to find the vehicle and the child.

Despite two days passing, no ransom demands have been made, leaving the motive for the kidnapping unclear.

According to police headquarters, between January and July, 474 GDs were filed for missing children aged 1-9, with 68 still missing.

For children aged 10-17, 15,243 GDs were filed in the same period, with 1,970 still missing, totaling 2,038 missing children in that age range.
